#2855. The Day After the Day After: The Houston Texans bolt past the LA Chargers 44-22

The Day After the Day After…when the raw, immediate emotions from the aftermath of a game diminish into the realm of clarity and the proverbial (or literal) hangover no longer haunts the mind. With that, a review of Week 9

Get right game (part deux): It might be harder to find a better opponent to face after a bye than the shockingly (pun somewhat intended) bad Chargers. While the Texans have underperformed based on preseason expectations, they are not like the Chargers. A fellow pre-season playoff contender, the Chargers opened the season 0-7. Catching a mercurial Texans team might have afforded them a chance to steal a win and salvage some pride in the season. Instead, this game went about as well as the Texans could hope for and then some. Houston put up a franchise-tying 44 points on the road, Stroud threw for 5 TDs and the defense got 8 sacks and 2 turnovers. Even the running game logged over 100 combined yards. All was not perfect, and Houston isn't immediately back on the road to the Super Bowl, but this game checked a lot of boxes for Houston's rebound hopes. Houston's first get-well game came at the Titans to get off the winless streak. A second road-beatdown was a well-needed salve to start the second half of the schedule.

Using the pass to set up the run: At times, it felt like the biggest problem for Stroud was not having enough footballs to throw around to all his receivers. 6 receivers had at least 2 receptions and over 20 yards receiving. Dell had his best game since he injured his leg at Kansas City in 2024, Boutte had a career day stretching the field and Collins merely added a catch-of-the-year option. Houston is never going to abandon the ground game but given that the offense moves more effectively through the air, the Texans might do well to favor the pass. Does it put pressure on the defense, especially if the team has multiple quick possessions? Yes. However, with the talent in the passing game and the noted shortfalls of the running game, Houston needs to play to their strengths. If nothing else, you borrow the Bill Walsh philosophy to use the pass to set up the run. Houston was more effective rushing the ball in the second half (69 yards vs. 35 1st half yards). With the Chargers needing to focus on limiting heavy aerial production, a decent ground game with Marks and company found a way to move the ball for effective gains.

Trades all done?: At the time of publication, the Texans hadn't added any new players via trade. If rumors are correct, the Texans are looking at help at the RB and safety position. Most might dream of Taylor, Barkley or Henry in the backfield, but would Houston want to pay up with their limited 2027/28 Draft capital for a back that is going to already stress a team that is going to be well over the cap at the start of the offseason. Pitre's return aided the defensive backfield, but Blankenship's absence and struggles are still issues. Plus, safety depth could help a squad that needs special teams reinforcements. While Caserio fears no trade, it does not seem likely that Houston will make another big move trade-wise (unlike division rival Jacksonville, which made some major trades in the past 36 hours to aid the defense).

6:43, 2nd Quarter, HOU Ball @ HOU 37, 2nd and 5; QB CJ Stroud with a deep pass to WR Tank Dell for a 63-yard TD.

Aside from the whole first-TD-in-almost-two-calendar-years-plotline, this play was actually critical to the game's momentum. The Chargers just cashed in on Stroud's INT to cut the deficit to 10-9. Houston, after scoring 10 points on their first two drives, had a punt and an INT on the next two. They needed to get something going. After a short 5-yard pass to Harrison, Houston set up in a shotgun passing formation. Dell, lined up in the slot on the right side, ran and out-and-up pattern, just getting behind the Chargers DB. Stroud hit Dell in stride with a deep strike, allowing Dell to sprint straight to end zone. While Houston would be forced to punt on its next possession, this TD seemed to uplift the overall play of the team, as it was the start of a 28-0 run in the game.

12: Total number of TFLs for the Texans: This is what most expected from the Houston defense this year. This tied the Houston franchise for 3rd-most in a single game (@ TEN in 2023). The franchise record is 15, set against Seattle in 2009. The most in the Ryans' regime: 14, against TEN in 2024.

2-1: Record in 2026 when Houston rushes for over 100 yards in a game. When we talk about Houston leaning into its effective passing game, this might be a counter to that. You can't not run the ball (this isn't the run-and-shoot), but finding that balance is critical. Play to your strengths, and if the passing game is doing its job, the running game will follow.

WR Tank Dell: 4 receptions/105 yards/1 TD. Welcome back Mr. Dell. We've missed you. Now, about cleanly catching those punts…

QB CJ Stroud: An INT…really? Well, he did make up for it with a 21-of-35/384 yard/5 TD day. I suppose that is adequate enough for a game ball.

Texans DL: Logged 7 of the team's 8 sacks and 9 of the teams 12 TFLs. Anderson, Clowney and Rankins are the first trio of Texans to ever record at least 2.0 sacks each in a single game.

CB Kamri Lassiter: 2 tackles (1 solo)/1 TFL/4 PDs: If anyone needed a bounce-back game, it was Lassiter. Was he perfect? No (arguably the miscommunication on the Chargers' 4th and 1 was more about miscommunication vs. individual corner play) but on this day, he looked more like the top CB2 of 2025 than whatever that was to start the 2026 season. Would be nice if he kept up that level of play.

SHOULD BE FORCED TO PRESS ALL OF JIM HARBAUGH'S KHAKIS WHILE LISTENING TO HIS INANE PRESS CONFERENCES ON REPEAT:

Texans punting game: If there was a part of the game that didn't look all that great, it was the punting game. Only needed for 3 attempts, but Kroeger's two first half punts are best not dwelt upon. Tank Dell, for all his receiving goodness, muffed a punt in the 1st half that could have seriously altered the momentum of the game. At least the squad didn't allow the Chargers to even attempt a return. However, that part of the game is going to have to pick it up in the weeks ahead.

Chargers OC Mike McDaniel: The Chargers did finally snap a 37 non-TD possession streak against the Texans, but that came in the 4th quarter of a game the Texans lead 38-9. The Chargers did add another TD, but aside from impacting the betting lines, the offense did not look good at all. Yes, LA was missing Ladd McConkey, but the team had struggled even with him on the field. Herbert still looks out of sorts and the McDaniel scheme with this offensive roster is the NFL version of square peg meets round hole. This first, and possibly only season in LA has been sheer [KITTEN] for McDaniel.

The Texans, 3-5, continue their road trip with a jaunt to Cleveland to face the 5-4 Browns (and a few familiar faces). Kickoff is slated for this coming Sunday at noon CST on Fox

#2853. ‘Gotham deserve better’: NWSL’s top team has to settle for 5k-seat stadium for historic semifinal

After a wide-ranging weekend of NWSL quarterfinals, the focus should be on who will book a place in the championship match on Nov. 21 in Washington, D.C.

Will the Utah Royals' tactical precision give them an edge over the domineering Washington Spirit? After suffering an upset in last year's quarterfinal against Gotham FC, can the Kansas City Current rewrite their story?

Questions like that should be driving the NWSL buzz as another year of expansion, broken records and a peculiar number of red cards bounds toward its climax. These discussions should light up group chats and warrant another round of something mulled and spiced, interspersed with watch party planning and prediction tinkering.

Instead, the presiding topics have been about poor field quality, small stadiums, unfair compromises and the logistical labyrinth that has been the NWSL's efforts to secure suitable venues for two of its biggest teams ahead of their semifinal matches.

Thanks to favorable negotiations and a willing sponsor, the No. 3 Spirit get to play the Royals at Audi Field. Their home stadium (which is owned by D.C. United in Major League Soccer) was initially scheduled to host an NCAA Division III college football game, which would have required the Spirit to relocate their playoff match to Northwest Stadium in Landover, Md., home of the Washington Commanders.

Not ideal for a fanbase behind the nickname "Rowdy Audi".

Still, no team is more hard done by this ordeal than Gotham FC, the No. 1 team in the league. They have already endured two matches on a home field so gnarled that they incurred a $10,000 fine for poor conditions. Like the Spirit, Gotham are not primary tenants at Sports Illustrated Stadium and are thus not in control of maintaining the pitch. On Monday, the league announced Gotham's semifinal would kick off at the 5,000-capacity Icahn Stadium on Randall's Island in Manhattan, 25 miles, an hour and 13 minutes away from Harrison on public transit and one-fifth the size of their New Jersey home.

Last week, the excitement of the NWSL playoffs were sullied by the early kickoff times. This week, it's the location of the games. At the heart of both issues is a harsh reality that defines the relationship between most NWSL teams and their home venues, and that of women's relationship to male counterparts historically across many cultures: mercy.

They are defending champions and won their first NWSL Shield this season. They edged out tennis star Coco Gauff's 2023 U.S. Open campaign to break an attendance record for women's sporting events in NYC in the middle of the men's World Cup this summer. They kept 15 clean sheets and conceded the fewest goals of any other team in the NWSL, despite dealing with a slew of injuries to their backline. Gotham's system is so well-oiled that head coach Juan Carlos Amorós was able to take five weeks' parental leave, placing assistant-turned-interim head coach Shaun Harris in charge. The team remained unbeaten when Amorós returned to the office. On Monday, he earned his third Coach of the Year nomination in the last four years.

Gotham's roster is a spoil of world-class talent. Some of those same decorated players have been able to indulge in the cauldron of culture that is NYC, making cameos on Broadway and attending New York Fashion Week shows.

Two of the last three NWSL Rookie of the Year awards have been awarded to Gotham players, in line with the number of championships they have won in the same period.

Those are just the team's accolades over the past few years. Zoom further out and consider how far they have come from their days as Sky Blue FC. Their growth as a club becomes even more impressive. The team had won only a single game in its entire season nine years ago, and now many would argue that they are in dynastic territory.

But we shouldn't get too hung up on meritocracy; any team that reaches the postseason in one of the most competitive leagues in the world should be able to play in the venue their seed dictates. Gotham FC's accomplishments — not to mention their ambitions — are so much bigger than a 5,000-capacity stadium. Their supporters deserve the chance to turn their stadium into a fortress that sends chills down the spines of their opponents.

Perhaps the worst part of all of this is that the owners and primary tenants of Sports Illustrated Stadium, New York Red Bulls, could have made this right. Their season ended on Oct. 17, a 10th-place finish in the league's eastern conference. They scheduled a home friendly for Saturday, Nov. 14 against Mexican side Club América.

That should have allowed Gotham to play at Sports Illustrated on Sunday, one of two broadcast windows the NWSL had for its semifinal, but as Sunday proved, the field conditions needed to be improved first. Only the Red Bulls could approve Gotham's proposals, but the two could not reach an accord.

Gotham lead owner Carolyn Tisch Blodgett said in a statement Monday that the club had "exhausted every possible avenue before making this decision." She reiterated that "players deserve a playing surface that meets the standards of a professional semifinal, and our fans deserve the opportunity to support them."

Red Bulls responded with their own statement saying the field is consistently quality-checked and has passed each of those. The MLS team, which will still play its friendly on Nov. 14, wished the NWSL team good luck.

The veil of disrespect is so thin that it will only motivate Gotham and its fanbase, but the source of that passion should be coming from a sporting place, not a systemic one. Women's sports hasn't fully emerged from the shadow of the WNBA Finals debacle in Atlanta — and until teams' successes are no longer treated as extraordinary events but events to respect and plan around, these shadows will continue to loom.

#2852. Luka Doncic ruthlessly trolls Hawks fans over franchise’s biggest mistake: ‘You could have had me’

Luka Dončić didn't just beat the Hawks on Monday night. He reminded their fans of the biggest mistake in franchise history.

During the Lakers' 124-114 victory, Dončić engaged in a hilarious courtside exchange with Hawks fans, reminding them that Atlanta once held the keys to his basketball future before foolishly trading them away.

"You all wish you would have had me. You all wish, huh?" Dončić taunted, according to a video shared on Threads by @RKessler23.

"No we don't, I've never wanted you," another insisted.

Jalen Johnson of the Atlanta Hawks and Luka Doncic of the Los Angeles Lakers hug after a game on Monday, Nov. 9, 2026, at State Farm Arena in Atlanta. NBAE via Getty Images

Dyson Daniels of the Atlanta Hawks and Luka Doncic of the Los Angeles Lakers hug after a game on Monday, Nov. 9, 2026, at State Farm Arena in Atlanta. NBAE via Getty Images

At least one Atlanta fan was willing to admit the painful truth.

"I wish we did, I do," the fan responded.

"You know you could have had me," Dončić reminded them.

"He's right," the person recording acknowledged through laughter.

The exchange reopened a wound from the 2018 NBA Draft, when Atlanta selected Dončić third overall before trading him to the Mavericks in a deal involving Trae Young.

Dončić eventually led Dallas to the NBA Finals, while Young has since landed in Washington alongside former Lakers star Anthony Davis.

Luka Doncic of the Los Angeles Lakers reacts after a 124-114 win over the Atlanta Hawks at State Farm Arena in Atlanta on Monday, Nov. 9, 2026. Getty Images

Monday's performance only added insult to injury.

Dončić torched the Hawks for 32 points, 10 assists, eight rebounds, five steals and two blocks, becoming the first Lakers player to record multiple games with at least 30 points, five assists, five steals and two blocks.

Not even Magic Johnson or Kareem Abdul-Jabbar accomplished that twice.

With Dončić leading the NBA in scoring at 40.1 points per game and Los Angeles sitting atop the standings at 10-2, his argument was difficult to dispute.

Now, eight years later and wearing a Lakers jersey, Dončić is still making the Hawks pay for their mistake.

#2851. Millions of dollars poured into prediction markets on election night, trading on Democratic control of Congress and Texas governor's race

More than 87% of all election markets across Kalshi and Polymarket gave the right candidate at least a 90% chance of winning their race 24 hours before election night, a CNBC analysis found.

Election night showed how traders reacted to real-time midterm results, as trading activity surged and market prices shifted to Democrats after results from Indiana began rolling in before 7 p.m. on Nov. 3. Many midterm races were uncompetitive, which boosted the overall hit rate on prediction markets.

"I'd say prediction markets did pretty well," said Koleman Strumpf, a professor of economics at Wake Forest University. "But they didn't outperform the best," he added, referring to traditional forecast polls that tracked results that night.

Odds and gambling platforms do not use methodologies used by traditional political polling, and therefore are not substitutes for political polls.

Prediction markets saw big trades on election night.

After 8 p.m. on Nov. 3, at least $1 million was traded on a Kalshi market that incumbent Gov. Greg Abbott would be reelected. Abbott eventually lost to Democrat Gina Hinojosa by more than 700,000 votes, according to the Associated Press. A little after 11 p.m. on election night, more than $1.4 million was traded on Kalshi that Republicans would not secure control of the House of Representatives.

Following the midterms, both Polymarket CEO Shayne Coplan and Kalshi CEO Tarek Mansour were on the social media platform X crediting prediction markets for correctly predicting races. Nate Silver, a political forecaster and founder of the Silver Bulletin newsletter, disputed the claim, arguing forecast models influenced prediction market movement. Silver joined Polymarket as an advisor in 2024.

"Prediction market probabilities strongly converged toward [our models] in individual Senate and gubernatorial races," Silver wrote on Silver Bulletin. "I was tracking this stuff closely, precisely because I envisioned that we might wind up in this sort of debate where prediction markets are low-key stealing valor from the models."

Prediction market volume on midterm election-related contracts across Kalshi and Polymarket more than tripled from the last week of October into the midterms week, according to a CNBC analysis of data published on Predictions.com. The data did not include combo markets, which bundle multiple contracts and pay out only if every leg resolves in the trader's favor.

Still, volume on midterm contracts pales in comparison with sports volume, which remains larger than all other categories.

Kalshi exceeded $3 billion in total midterm contract volume, according to the platform's website, which also includes volume for contracts on mayoral races. Last week, Polymarket's two exchanges reported nearly $700 million in volume for midterm contracts.

While prediction markets broadly anticipated Democratic control of Congress, the blue tsunami is expected to bite the industry in other ways.

Three days after the midterms, Sen. Adam Schiff, D-Calif, criticized the federal regulator responsible for the platforms, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, for allowing sports contracts.

"Sports prediction markets are sports bets. By effectively requiring prediction markets to offer contracts in all 50 states, even on Tribal lands, the CFTC is once again violating state law and Tribal sovereignty," Schiff wrote on X.

Disclosure: CNBC and Kalshi have a commercial relationship that includes customer acquisition and a minority investment.

#2850. Sean McVay on Puka Nacua injury: I'd be lying if I said I wasn't questioning that play call

Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua is set to go on injured reserve after suffering MCL, PCL and turf toe injuries in Sunday’s win over the Commanders.

Nacua’s injuries occurred on the Rams’ final offensive play when he was tackled after rushing for five yards on third-and-11. Nacua took a handoff on the play and head coach Sean McVay was asked at a Monday press conference if he second-guessed himself for putting Nacua in position to take a hit at that point in the game.

McVay said he’s “kicking myself about those kinds of things” and called it something the Rams have to think about “internally” as they move forward.

“I’d be lying to you if I said I haven’t questioned the decision-making on that last play over and over in my head of what could have been another option that you felt like could have gotten a conversion, and maybe ended the game that would’ve led to him not taking a violent hit to his right knee,” McVay said. “It’s stuff that I feel tremendous responsibility for, and we’ve got to be able to figure out how to protect these guys while also putting them in positions that help our team and allow them to be able to shine. He’s a guy we have to be intentional about because it’s a bummer. Because he can do so much, you want to make sure you don’t take that for granted.”

With Nacua and Davante Adams now out for the indefinite future, the Rams may be in the market for receiving help before the trade deadline passes at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday. They do not have their 2027 first- or third-round picks, their 2028 second-round pick or their 2029 third-round pick thanks to their trades for Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie.

#2849. Eagles News: ESPN says Jordan Davis trade is a disaster for the Jaguars

Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation!

I really like Jordan Davis. I wanted the Eagles to draft him and I enjoyed rooting for him. But taking what the Jacksonville Jaguars offered for him was a no-brainer. There were people talking about the Eagles potentially getting trade offers for Jalen Carter for a similar price of a first-round pick and a second-round pick. To get that for Davis, who is a lesser player who isn't trusted to play as much as Carter … it's insane. Howie Roseman clearly overpaid Davis but he's very good at not doubling down on mistakes and instead making his wrongs right. Well done by the Eagles. Very interested to see how they utilize their draft picks to help spark the next era of success.

Let's get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links …

NFL trade deadline grades: Deals for Jordan Davis, Jessie Bates III, Andre Cisco – ESPN

There's no other way to start this: This trade is a disaster for Jacksonville. The Jaguars are absolutely right to go for it. Entering Monday, they had a 12.8% chance to win the Super Bowl, per ESPN's Football Power Index, second highest of any team and best in the AFC. And that's why I was OK with them rolling the dice on Jessie Bates III earlier in the day. A late-round pick for Davon Godchaux, too? Fine. But first- and second-round picks for Davis? Reckless would be putting it mildly. The numbers do not paint a picture of Davis being someone who is worth anywhere near that type of trade compensation. He has played 52% of snaps for the Eagles. That number is not particularly unusual for a run-stuffing nose tackle, but that's exactly the point: The Jaguars just dealt first- and second-round picks for a part-time player who helps only against the run! There is no world where that is worth it. Davis has a run stop win rate in the 71st percentile among interior defenders this season. He was in the 93rd percentile in 2025 and the 52nd percentile in 2024. This season, he has a 13.5% run stop rate — the rate at which a player records a tackle on a run that resulted in a successful play for the defense by EPA — per NFL Next Gen Stats, 14th best among defensive tackles with at least 100 run defense snaps and just behind former Eagles teammate Moro Ojomo. In other words, he has been a good run defender, not elite.

Eagles are stockpiling draft picks through 2029 – BGN

The Eagles surprised just about everyone when it was announced that they were trading Jordan Davis to the Jaguars ahead of the NFL trade deadline, but they got a huge return for their defensive tackle, including a first-round draft pick in 2027 and a second-round pick in 2029. Those two acquistions give Howie Roseman 10 total picks in the first two rounds over the next three drafts, 26 total projected through all rounds. That's insane!

Jordan Davis trade grades: Jaguars-Eagles blockbuster as Jags load up for Super Bowl run – SB Nation

Philadelphia Eagles grade: A. I am always going to give a big-time writer's tilt when it comes to teams accepting the position they're in. When news first emerged that the Jaguars traded a 1st and 2nd for an Eagles DT we all assumed at SB Nation that Jacksonville was getting Jalen Carter, not Jordan Davis. Philly gave up a player they can replace and got a significant return. This was a very smart move for a team that doesn't have a shot in 2026 and is playing for next year. Their picks in 2027 can help address their much larger need concerns along the offensive line, and simply improve the team from the bottom up — which needs to happen. This is an example of an incredibly well-oiled franchise taking advantage of a team desperate to make an impact. It wasn't neccesarily a seller's market on run stopping DTs, but they made it one anyway.

Another trade! Jaguars land their defensive game-changer in Jordan Davis – Big Cat Country

There's always a danger in handing out top grades for blockbuster trades. Draft capital matters, and surrendering a first and second-round pick is a considerable commitment. But the Jaguars have a genuine opportunity to do something special this season. They've lost important defensive starters to injury, identified the positions that need strengthening and gone out to acquire established NFL talent. Godchaux brings experience. Bates brings leadership and playmaking ability. Davis brings size, power, youth and the potential to anchor the defensive interior for the foreseeable future. Most importantly, these additions complement a roster that was already performing at an exceptionally high level. James Gladstone and Liam Coen clearly believe this team is ready to compete for the biggest prize in football. Rather than sitting back and hoping their existing roster is good enough, they've invested heavily in making sure it is. This is what going ALL IN looks like. The Jaguars have made their intentions abundantly clear, and the rest of the league have just been put on notice.

NFL trade grades: Jaguars overpay for Jordan Davis while going all in on Super Bowl chase – The Athletic

Eagles grade: A+. This is an impressive return for Roseman, and the Eagles are now loaded with future draft capital. They now have two first-round picks in 2027, and two first-round picks in 2028, their own and the Patriots' pick from the A.J. Brown trade. They also own two second-round picks in 2029. That is a ton of ammunition to use in whatever fashion Roseman sees fit. They could stick and pick. They could trade any of those picks for veteran players. They could package them to move around in the draft. As our Jonathan Jones wrote in our trade deadline live blog, "What the Eagles have now is total optionality." This clears the way for the Eagles to extend Ojomo, who is on the final year of his rookie deal. It is always difficult to hand out three large contracts to one position group. The Eagles are also paying Jalen Carter a top-of-market contract. They will incur a palatable dead-money charge of $15.4 million for Davis in 2027, according to figures from Over The Cap. Roseman is doing the right thing, turning a losing season into future opportunity.

NFL trade grades: Evaluating every deal made ahead of the 2026 deadline – NFL.com

Davis has been a good run defender for his career, but his 13.5% run-stop rate this season ranks 14th among DTs with a minimum of 100 run plays defended — behind teammate Moro Ojomo, I should add — with a 1.8 run stuff percentage (T-58th). Last year, before he got paid, was his best season with a 16.5% run-stop rate (fourth among DTs) with a run stuff rate of 4.3%, behind that of DaVon Hamilton, whom he's essentially been brought in to replace. There is the risk for the Jags. It feels like a knee-jerk reaction to Hamilton's injury led to a massive overpay. Davis can be a good player, stuff the middle and can provide a little more pop for a nose tackle in the passing game. However, a first-round pick and a future second? We know DTs have been scarce in this market, but paying that much for a run defender is a lot. But what do I know. Maybe DC Anthony Campanile sees something in Davis that he can unlock. Maybe the Jags really just believe that stuffing the run and eating up blockers so they can get to third-and-long is worth that investment. Maybe next to Josh Hines-Allen and Travon Walker we'll get a better version. Maybe Davis, having heard all the negative chatter about how the Jags overpaid for him, will be motivated and bring a wrecking-ball attitude to Duval and storm his way through the postseason on a mission. For me, that's a lot of maybes to hang a first- and second-rounder on.

Jaguars may plan for Jordan Davis to play more than 52 percent of the time – PFT

In nine starts this season, Davis has been on the field for 52 percent of the defensive plays. Given what the Jaguars have given up to get him (next year's first-round pick and a second-round selection in 2029), Jacksonville may be planning to increase his workload. Unless the Jaguars make him a three-down player, it will be a massive investment for a run-stopping defensive tackle. And it explains the Eagles' position that the Jaguars made an offer that Philly couldn't refuse.

Five thoughts on the Eagles, Howie Roseman trading Jordan Davis to Jacksonville Jaguars – PHLY Eagles

Clearing the runway for Ojomo. Aside from the draft capital acquired, the next big ripple effect from the trade is the pathway it clears for the Eagles to sign 25-year-old defensive tackle Moro Ojomo to a contract extension before free agency opens this offseason. Many wondered if Ojomo would be the interior rusher the Eagles traded going into Tuesday's deadline because the team's commitment in Davis and Jalen Carter made the former seventh-round pick the odd man out. Instead, the team should now have the flexibility to pay Ojomo near the top of the market and plan for the partnership between him and Carter to serve as the foundation for the defensive front in the coming years. Given the way this year played out, Roseman's decision to pivot was likely the correct one and is more in line with what we've seen the general manager prefer in the past. Whether it was Javon Hargrave next to Fletcher Cox or Milton Williams next to Carter for the team's run to Super Bowl LIX, the best version of the Eagles pass rushes under Roseman have featured a dynamic pass rusher next to a superstar defensive tackle to overload opposing offensive lines having to choose which one to double team.

The Eagles can now afford to keep Ojomo around. They can put the franchise tag on him or re-sign him to a long term deal. Ojomo and Carter will give the Eagles a pair of highly disruptive DTs to build the defense around. I thought Ojomo played two of his best games over the past two weeks. He's also seen as a good fit in the locker room. He is the kind of player you want to keep around. As far as this season, this will mean more snaps for Byron Young and Ty Robinson. I'll be interested to see if the Eagles add Gabe Hall or Zion Wilson from the practice squad. Hall is the better athlete. Wilson is more of the run-stuffing type and could be a better fit if they want a NT.

A couple Eagles players react to news of Jordan Davis trade – NBCSP

Not only was Jordan Davis a former first-round pick and the anchor of the Eagles' defensive line. He was a team captain and a favorite in the locker room. So it wasn't easy for his teammates to find out about the trade. "It hit me hard," Hunt said to NBC Sports Philadelphia's John Clark on Monday night. "I got like eight messages on my phone seeing if I'm OK. I'm not on social media, so I didn't see anything. And then I saw the messages and found out. I texted him pretty much instantly. But it sucks. Because it's a part of the business and it's part of what just has to happen sometimes. I hate the move but I trust whatever Howie got going."

6 potential Patriots targets ahead of the NFL trade deadline – Pats Pulpit

EDGE Nolan Smith. The 2-7 Eagles continued to move pieces ahead of the trade deadline Monday, sending defensive tackle Jordan Davis to Jacksonville in exchange for a first- and second-round pick. Could former first-round pick Nolan Smith be next? Despite the Eagles' struggles, the 25-year-old has been productive, leading the team with 21 pressures this season while remaining a physical run defender. Philadelphia also exercised Smith's fifth-year option this past offseason, keeping him under contract through 2027 with under $14 million in cash owed his way. His age, production and contractual control could make him an appealing addition, although it may take a more significant investment than other names on this list.

Eagles name SportsRadio 94WIP broadcast booth at Lincoln Financial Field after Merrill Reese – PhiladelphiaEagles.com

The Eagles weren't done celebrating Merrill Reese's 50 seasons from the broadcast booth. During a special halftime ceremony, a tribute video recounting the best highlights from the past 50 seasons played on the videoboard and the legends who made those plays happen were on the field. Reese's partner and color analyst for the past 28 seasons – Eagles Hall of Fame wide receiver Mike Quick – pre-recorded a message that played to the fans to announce that the SportsRadio 94WIP broadcast booth will now be named the Merrill Reese Broadcast Booth going forward.

Jordan Davis trade shows why Giants need to capitalize on 2026 opportunity – Big Blue View

The Philadelphia Eagles' trade on Monday of defensive tackle Jordan Davis to the Jacksonville Jaguars is a perfect illustration of why the 5-2-1 New York Giants need to take advantage of the opportunity they have in the NFC East this season. The Eagles have won the division in three of the past four years, with two Super Bowl appearances and one title along the way. They won't win it this time around. They are now 2-7 and riding a seven-game losing streak after Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants. They are as far down as an Eagles team has been since 2020, when Philadelphia went 4-11-1. You have to know, though, that general manager Howie Roseman is not going to let the Eagles stay down.

Cowboys at Colts Stock Report: Caleb Downs, Quinnen Williams excel – Blogging The Boys

Stock Up: Christian Parker. This is also a "nowhere to go but up" situation, and the quality of the opponent is certainly worth keeping in mind. But let's say that Christian Parker's defense generated eight different stops on Sunday, including the one that sealed the game in Caleb Downs' interception. Is this representative of a turning tide? That would be a huge leap to make. But it is definitely representative of a group that is getting better and that is awesome to see.

NFC Hierarchy/Obituary: Week 10 edition – PhillyVoice

10) Cowboys (4-5): The Cowboys barely survived a clearly tanking Colts team on Sunday. But they're in pretty big danger of falling too far behind the Giants this week. They'll face an old nemesis in the 49ers, while the Giants are at home against the Commanders. They're already two games back with a head-to-head loss to the Giants. If they lose on Sunday and the Giants win, that might be too insurmountable a deficit to overcome.

Commanders vs. Giants Monday injury report: Lucas Patrick in concussion protocol – Hogs Haven

Commanders veteran Lucas Patrick has provided stability at the center spot, which was a point of chaos and poor performance before he was signed on Sept. 16. Nick Allegretti and rookie Matt Gulbin struggled before he got to Washington and when called to action, including Sunday's loss to the L.A. Rams. That happened because Patrick suffered a concussion during the game and is now in the protocol. That puts his availability for Thursday's game at the New York Giants in serious jeopardy. He was a DNP on the Monday injury report leading into that game, though it's important to note that it was only an estimation because the Commanders didn't conduct a formal workout.

Vikings Week 9 Stock Market Report – Daily Norseman

Carson Wentz. Honestly, the average fan could have played quarterback better than Wentz did on Monday night. In the second half, he completed more passes to Bills than Vikings. His adjusted completion percentage was 37%. That means only about one of every three passes was accurate. That's off-the-charts bad- even for a backup. Should the Vikings trade for a quarterback (which they desperately need to do) Wentz should be cut. It's inexcusable for a veteran quarterback like Wentz to be that bad and still be employed. He squandered an excellent performance by the Vikings defense and cost the Vikings a valuable win in a tight division by being totally unprepared and awful in his 101st and hopefully last game as a professional- at least with the Vikings.

The Raiders defense allowed 38 points in the loss to the 49ers on Sunday, the sixth consecutive game of giving up 30-plus points. But coach Klint Kubiak said Monday that he does not anticipate changes to the defense, giving defensive coordinator Rob Leonard a vote of confidence.

#2847. “Doesn’t Hurt That You Have $50M+”: Kyle Whittingham Shifts Attention to Oregon’s Massive Recruiting Budget Ahead of Ducks Clash

Michigan football is at a crossroads as it aims to rescue its college football season, and the pressure is on Kyle Whittingham. The Wolverines' head coach made the decision to fire offensive coordinator Jason Beck after an unsatisfactory run of performances, but he still needs to win games to keep his own job secure.

Ahead of the game against the Oregon Ducks, who are themselves turning a corner after some tough results, Whittingham shifted attention to Oregon's massive recruiting budget, highlighting the difference between the two sides.

"He really does a great job recruiting and it doesn't hurt that you have $50+ million dollars at your disposal to, in essence outbid everybody. Not everybody, but a lot of people. But that's not his fault," Whittingham said about head coach Dan Lanning to reporters, via Inside Michigan.

He further said that he meant it as a credit to the program and its desire to focus on young athletes in the NIL era.

"That's a credit. I mean, that's a credit to their program and their dedication and desire to win and the support they have. NIL is the name of the game in recruiting these days. It's shifted so much," he went on.

After a tough defeat to Michigan State, offensive coordinator Jason Beck received his marching orders from Kyle Whittingham, and he addressed the decision to media personnel.

"Well, watching the film really was the deciding factor, and I had the intention of waiting until after the season, as I mentioned," Whittingham said to reporters, as reported by Wolverines Wire.

He further revealed when it became completely clear to him that a change was needed.

"But when I turned the film on and really dove into it, it just became apparent to me that you need to make the change now. And there's just too much regression in the offense in that particular game. And that's what led to the decision."

The decision will be put to the test as the Wolverines play the Oregon Ducks on Saturday.

#2845. A massive trade in Nvidia just went off – here are the details

The biggest options trade on Nvidia stock Monday seems to think the controversy swirling around the chip leader and its embattled CEO is creating a buying opportunity.In a trade about an hour after the opening bell that involved more than $100 million in options premium, someone exchanged an existing call spread for a more bullish position that captures the next five months of trading in Nvidia.The core position was the purchase of 52,000 195-strike calls expiring Feb. 19 worth about $57 million – contracts the trader opened for a new long position while simultaneously selling the same number of 245-strike calls for the same expiry, lowering the cost of the trade by $10 million. The net position, a bullish call spread, needs Nvidia to trade above around $206 by expiry, or about 15% higher, to be profitable. If Nvidia stock reaches the short, 245-strike call, it would represent a nearly 40% rally and return the stock to its all-time high of $243, that was reached on October 6th.The trade was likely part of a "roll" down from an existing 210/255-strike call spread worth about $42 million that was closed out, according to SpotGamma analysis.

"The person got more aggressive rolling this spread down to lower strikes to get more upside exposure by getting higher delta," SpotGamma founder Brent Kochuba said by phone. "They're trading the call spread here because the vol is expensive going into earnings. It's a significant increase in upside delta exposure."Delta is options parlance for describing how quickly an options price will react to a change in the underlying stock price. The trader's updated position, taken at lower strikes, will make money faster if Nvidia rallies. In other words, it's a higher conviction trade that the chipmaker's stock will soon rebound. The 195-strike calls they bought for $57 million was the single biggest options trade on the tape Monday, according to SpotGamma. Of the top 20 options trades by dollar-amount, 12 were Nvidia, the data show.Flows around the stock generally leaned bullish by midday, with 57% of options volume tied to calls and more than $660 million of call premium likely initiated by call-buyers, SpotGamma data show. The most popular single contract by volume was the 180-strike call expiring Monday, that needs Nvidia to recover 1.2% by the bell to break even.

#2842. Rockets break the white unis losing streak against Denver 110-100

This won't be one of those 2,000 word recaps that I do at times. In fact, it will mark the season debut of Bullet Points – The Lazy Man's Friend(tm)

The Rockets lost the two previous game, which were by no means twins, due to the same issue, essentially. That is to say, bad shooting. Against Phoenix, the Rockets shot it so badly they didn't break 100 points. Not scoring 100 points in a modern NBA game usually spells defeat, but to the Rockets credit, they did hold the Suns to 102 points. The problem is they shot 36-94 overall, for 39%, and 10-35 from three point range, for 29%. They did make their freethrows at around 90%. The game before that, against the Timberwolves, it was much the same story. 43% overall, 35% from three. When the Rockets can't shoot it from outside, they will typically lose. Why? Generally because there is one player who can get to the basket and do anything there regularly, Alperen Sengun. If he isn't doubled, or he's neutralized, it can be a long night of no one open for the Rockets.

Tonight featured the Rockets against a Denver team that just doesn't strike the same fear into opponents they did a few years ago. Still, they were 5-3 coming into tonight, which doesn't sound great, but would, if extrapolated to a full season, come to about 50 wins. 5 of 8 isn't bad in the NBA. Would the Rockets be able to hold Denver on defense, which they couldn't do against the TWolves. Could the Rockets score more than the paltry 99 they mustered against the Suns? Could they overcome the new, pinstriped, white jerseys they'd worn for all three losses.

In a word, yes, but it wasn't easy. It wasn't easy because the Rockets starting lineup more or less played the Nuggets even. Now, you might think that the Rockets would decide that despite the lack of success, they'd just keep doing the same thing. You'd only be partly right.

One of the Rockets big advantages over Denver seemed to be their depth. Denver just doesn't have much compared to the Rockets, who are nonetheless down three centers at the moment. The heavier bench lineups seemed to pull away from the Nuggets. This allowed the Rockets to go into halftime with a 14 point lead, which grew to as much as 19 before the Rockets hit one of those dreaded scoring lulls from last season, where what most would think of as their best lineup just can't score or defend.

So, did the Rockets keep at it, keep doing the things that cost them the lead? They did not. They went small, and pulled Alperen Sengun from the game. It's not that Alpie was bad, he was 9-17 for 20 points, 12 rebounds, 8assists to 2 turnovers, with a steal and a block. But the mobility edge, especially on defense, and running off misses, was pronounced.

The bench did good work, especially around the beginning of the fourth quarter. Tari Eason, in my opinion, continues to build a good case for 6th man of the year.

The Rockets ended up shooting it well. They shot 41 of 91 overall, for 45%, and 14 of 38 from three point range, for 37%. They didn't take a ton of freethrows, but made 14 of 17 for 82%. Denver shot 37 of 83 for 45% overall, but a woeful 8-29 from three point range (28%).

The Rockets absolutely crushed Denver on the offensive glass, 15 to 7, and that showed up in the Rockets attempting 8 more shots than the Nuggets. It wasn't an especially high paced game by modern standards, but Denver plays currently at the slowest pace in the NBA, and if an opponent counters that with extra chances, they can get into trouble, as we say tonight.

It's great to break the Curse of The New White Jerseys after so short a run. Now that's been proven, we don't need to see them again.

The Rockets are 8-3, which currently has them essentially in a tie for 3rd place in the "Why are you looking at the standings in early November?" stakes.

The picture with this article is Alpie rejecting Jokic, which means any comparisons are over. Alpie wins.

#2839. Bills-Vikings game carries major significance for both teams

The Bills and Vikings have identical 0-4 records in the Super Bowl. They enter Monday night’s game with identical 6-1 records.

And the stakes are very high for both teams.

For Buffalo, which hopes to force the January road to SoFi Stadium through the open-air new venue in Western New York, it’s important to maintain distance between the 6-2 Jaguars and 7-2 Broncos. (The division is looking like the Bills’ to lose, with the Patriots now at 5-4.)

For Minnesota, their status as the last unbeaten team in the NFL could dissolve to being the last team out of the NFC playoff picture.

The NFC North, which now has a 20-3 record outside the division, has the Vikings at 6-1, the Bears at 7-2, the Lions are 6-2, and the Packers at 6-3. (Combined, they’ve lost as many games as the 0-8 Chargers.)

Last week, when the Vikings picked up their first loss of the season, the Lions, Bears, and Packers won. This week, the Lions, Bears, and Packers have won. A loss by the Vikings would conclude a two-week window in which the Vikings are 0-2, and the rest of the division is 6-0.

It gets worse. The 49ers, Seahawks, and Rams each won on Sunday. In the end, five playoff berths will go to the four teams of the NFC North and top three teams of the NFC West.

Two of those teams will be left out. And, frankly, the Vikings seem destined to be one of them.

Even with a 6-2 record, if they lose to the Bills. Because even though the defense is good enough to win a Super Bowl, the offense isn’t good enough to win a playoff game. It could be just bad enough to keep the team from making the playoffs.

It was one thing for the Vikings’ defense to not gripe when the end result of each game was victory. If the second game of a four-week gauntlet doesn’t go Minnesota’s way (the Packers and 49ers are up next), things could get even more awkward in the locker room.

The problem is that, despite plenty of speculation and chatter, the Vikings don’t seem to be inclined to pull the cord on the emergency option of trading for Daniel Jones or Kirk Cousins. The organization’s chronic “just good enough is just good enough” vibe remains palpable.

Which means it all comes down to Carson Wentz against the Bills.

Could Minnesota win? When Buffalo last visited Minnesota in 2018, the Vikings entered the game as 17-point favorites. The Bills, fueled by then-rookie quarterback Josh Allen throwing for 196 yards and a touchdown and rushing for 39 yards and two touchdowns (including a hurdle over linebacker Anthony Barr), won the game easily, 27-6. (Last week, Allen said the leap over a linebacker was the moment he realized “I do belong here.”)

Four years ago, the Bills were favored by 6.5 points over the Vikings. Minnesota won a crazy game in overtime, 33-30, with Vikings receiver Justin Jefferson making the catch of the century on a fourth-down, game-on-the-line play.

Tonight, in many respects, the season is on the line for the Vikings. Especially if they won’t be trying to upgrade the most important position on the team, which in recent weeks has been the weakest on the roster.

#2838. Tokenization platform Securitize gains 10% postmarket on Q3 results, move into asset-backed finance

Tokenization platform Securitize climbed about 10% postmarket after reporting third quarter growth alongside increased operating expenses, and announcing an expansion into asset-backed finance through a strategic acquisition.

Miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively new corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure. Tokenized assets on the platform grew 9% in the third quarter, to $4.8 billion, from the same period a year ago. Aggregate transaction volume rose 20% from a year ago, to $4.3 billion. Revenue of $11.5 million was up 28% from last year.

The growth came as bullish sentiment around tokenization gained traction throughout the third quarter, ahead of the Security and Exchange Commission formalizing the long awaited Innovation Exemption on Sept. 17, which created a temporary pathway for trading of certain tokenized stocks and strengthened the regulatory outlook.

Profitability is still meaningfully below year-ago levels, due in part to costs associated with going public over the summer, as well as the scaling up of the tokenization business at an active time for the entire sector, Securitize CEO Carlos Domingo told CNBC in an exclusive interview.

Securitize reinforced "certain areas of the company like finance, compliance, legal [and] cybersecurity," which increased corporate costs "compared to a year ago when we were privately held," Domingo said. "We're in in a very good position. The adjusted EBITDA … is improving significantly from previous quarters."

Securitize reported an adjusted EBITDA loss of $2 million, compared with positive adjusted EBITDA of $3.6 million a year ago, better than a $5.5 million loss in the second quarter. The company posted a 183% increase in operating costs and expenses.

Also on Monday, the Securitize board authorized a $50 million share buyback and announced the acquisition of River One, an institutional asset-backed financing platform developing technology to connect stablecoin capital with traditional lending markets. Terms were not disclosed.

Securitize sees an opportunity to modernize the $9 trillion market for asset backed finance by using stablecoins to finance real world assets, generate yield and tokenize investment positions and credit products, Domingo said.The acquisition also marks an expansion beyond Securitize's core niche markets at a time when tokenization's competitive landscape is growing, with traditional asset managers like BlackRock and Franklin Templeton, and established financial market infrastructure providers like DTCC and Broadridge, entering the industry.

"We have been very active in tokenized funds, treasuries [and] yield … And we've been obviously recently very active in tokenized stocks, so this adds another piece of the puzzle in the emerging tokenization space for us to capture revenue growth."

#2836. Takeaways from Bills win over Vikings

The Buffalo Bills beat the Vikings 23-6 in Week 9 on Monday Night Football, a dominant defensive effort that paired wonderfully with fine performances from Josh Allen and James Cook.

The win moved Joe Brady's team to 7-1 on the season.

These are my takeaways from Buffalo's victory.

The Bills defense had an epic performance in this game, I don't care who the quarterback was. Carson Wentz was 8-of-25 for 81 yards with two picks. And the goalposts can't be moved here. While rumors have swirled of Minnesota trading for a quarterback this past week, there were many who believed the Vikings weren't really downgrading at the position going from Kyler Murray to Wentz for this primetime battle.

Let's not forget, in Week 1, in a relief appearance after Kyler Murray was injured, Wentz was 12-of-19 for 133 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions. On paper, as a veteran pocket passer, he should be better suited for Kevin O'Connell's offense.

And it's not as if Wentz had a pedestrian outing. He had a quarterback rating of 8.9 against the Bills defense. That's the lowest rating a quarterback with at least 25 attempts in a game has managed since… 2019.

Now, of course, Wentz missed on a handful of throws in this contest, but the Bills defense forced him to hold onto the football often — his 2.82-second average time to throw was higher than Josh Allen in this game — with outstanding coverage downfield for the vast majority of this matchup.

The pass rush and coverage were married throughout, and Buffalo only had to blitz on 25.9% of Wentz's dropbacks to affect the pocket consistently.

And I'll finish with this storyline that probably won't be talked about enough given how abysmal the Vikings pass game was — Minnesota ran it 12 times for 51 yards, which equates to a 4.3 yards-per-tote average. Aaron Jones averaged 3.2 yards per carry. Only 27.3% of the Vikings runs were successful — determined by yards gained relative to down and distance — the fifth-lowest rate for a run game in Week 9.

Buffalo's run defense is steadily improving each week, and it's already much more consistent than it was a season ago.

The stats will miss the sheer brilliance of Allen in this game. His rating was only 87.3. But beyond his slightly floated interception — that did come on a 3rd and 23, mind you — the Bills quarterback excelled against the most unique and aggressive defense in football, a truly elite unit, on its home turf.

To start 3-of-5 for 24 yards with a pick and finish the evening 21-of-31 for 234 with a touchdown through the air was immaculate from Allen.

He commanded the offense, both pre and post snap exactly how it should be done. He made smart decisions and threw with proper velocity/touch starting with that touchdown drive near the end of the first half. His ball placement was superb as well.

And, heck, no quarterback is going to be perfect for 60 minutes against that Vikings defense.

Allen did all this without Dion Dawkins and Alec Anderson.

MVP-caliber performance from him in this game.

Grable and Corbett allowed four pressures each. Not exactly what clubs want from starting blockers. But after a few miscommunications early that led to quick pressures, I thought both depth players settled in nicely, and really got after it in the run game in the second half.

The Brian Flores defensive scheme is designed to create offensive line miscommunication, and Grable and Corbett have never played alongside each other in an NFL game before.

But instead of their presence on the field becoming a story throughout this game, an issue that severely hampered the Bills offense all night, Grable and Corbett were steady in the second half, as run and pass blockers.

The responsibilities in Jim Leonhard's defense are starting to become second nature to Terrel Bernard, Dorian Williams, and Kaleb Elarms-Orr.

Williams and Bernard snagged a pick each in this one, and Bernard dropped probably the most gift-wrapped interception opportunity of his NFL career.

They are flowing freely in coverage, rapidly reacting to route concepts, and getting to proper depth at the intermediate level. Against the run, they're triggering quickly and regularly not allowing blocks to stick to them.

In this game, Bernard led the team with six tackles. Dorian Williams had three without a miss. And Elarms-Orr added three tackles of his own on just 13 snaps. This trio has become an underrated three-down group.

Sure, it wasn't idyllic to start. But once Brady understood the outside pitch plays weren't working on the ground, he went away from them.

Then, later, when he realized the interior run game was doing just enough to keep the Vikings defense on its heels and burn clock, he stuck with it.

But it wasn't a one-dimensional attack for Buffalo in this game. There was a fine collection of play-action, throws to tight ends in the flat, running backs involved through the air. Lots of 13 personnel. Over-the-middle looks for Khalil Shakir, some classic first-read looks outside for DJ Moore, and well-timed quick screens to receivers.

Again, it's never going to be flawless against a Flores defense that has the horses on the Vikings roster.

But Brady was in his bag as a play-caller in this convincing win.

Whether it was Tyler Bass making his 18th consecutive field goal (a team record) to begin the season, Tommy Doman Jr. handling punt and kickoff duties and laying the lumber to force a fumble, or Greg Dortch's big return to begin the game, special teams coordinator Jeff Rodgers has built a fantastic unit that was showcased in this Monday Night Football win.

In a low-scoring, defensive clash like we got in the first half, I can't stress enough how important Bass making those kicks was to avoid field-position and momentum shifts.

Doman even proved capable of kicking a "dirty ball" that hits within the landing zone but isn't immediately fielded by the returner.

Buffalo's special teams were once again stellar in victory.

#2834. Mike Brown’s lineup experiments are paying dividends for Knicks

At this stage in the season, winning isn't enough for the Knicks.

The champions care more about how they win.

"Obviously, we want to play well, we want to win, but we also want to continue to grow as a team and try not to plateau," Jalen Brunson said after practice Monday. "I think the way we do that is to continue to try to see how we can win games differently."

New York Knicks head coach Mike Brown directs his team against the Cleveland Cavaliers in Cleveland, Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026. AP Photo/Phil Long

That sentiment trickles down from head coach Mike Brown. Constant experimentation is a core staple to his philosophy. It feels like there's a surprise in the box score every game.

His players believe that brings the best out of them.

"It's kind of a freeing thing, playing that way, knowing that you don't have to really be looking over your shoulder or thinking that one thing is gonna ruin whatever," Landry Shamet said Monday. "And I think that he knows that we have that makeup as a group, too, that we're all on the same page in wanting the best for each other — the next man up kind of mentality. It's from top to bottom, and it's a good environment to have."

Brown used an 11-man rotation for Saturday's 109-97 win in Cleveland. That wasn't the result of garbage-time minutes, as all 11 saw the court in the first half. It was clear Brown wanted to get guys involved who are usually out of the rotation, such as Mohamed Diawara and Dalton Knecht.

It represents the biggest difference between Brown and predecessor Tom Thibodeau, who established a rotation and stuck strictly to it unless forced to change. Thibodeau prioritized maximizing his chances of winning every single night. Brown looks at the regular season more like a canvas to try new lineups, rotations and systems so that, by the end of the year, he has more available in his toolkit.

That process might be ugly at times, but it's designed to deliver long-term results.

Brown credits it as a big reason for their championship last season. The likes of Shamet and Jordan Clarkson spent time in and out of the rotation all year but stepped up in the postseason when their number was called. The shift to an offense built around Karl-Anthony Towns as a hub was only possible because they toyed with it during the regular season.

Landry Shamet #44 of the New York Knicks dribbles against the Cleveland Cavaliers on Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026, at Rocket Arena in Cleveland. NBAE via Getty Images

"It builds trust," Brown said Monday, "because it's like, 'Hey, they trust me to go out there and play right now, even though I might not have played in two or three games.' It helps with connectivity because guys feel more part of it, because they're getting an opportunity. It helps with everybody's readiness because the reality of it is, if a guy is sitting on the bench and he's been there game after game after game, which happens sometimes — I'm not saying that will never happen because it's gonna happen sometimes — then he may lose a little interest and relax a little bit because it's like, 'Hey, I'm not going in.' But then, if you call their number every once in a while, throw them in a game, now they know, 'Oh, I gotta be ready.' "

Even Jaden Akins, signed to a two-way deal like Knecht, has seen a little action beyond garbage time.

"If he can go in the game during some real moments," Brown said, "anybody can."

It's different from Thibodeau's final season, when he inserted Shamet and Delon Wright into the rotation out of desperation in the Eastern Conference final, having hardly used them previously.

Under Brown, there is a track record on which to fall back for everyone on the team, even if they go long stretches out of the rotation.

"It builds a lot, when you're talking about building a team," Brown said. "And then at the end of the day, your guys get used to it, so come playoff time, if you try something new or different when it comes to the lineups, it's not like, 'Oh my God, what's going on? We've never done this.' Nah, we've done it."

There is the flip side, though. Playing time and roles constantly are changing. Jose Alvarado started the year as the backup point guard but now finds himself behind Tyler Kolek in the pecking order after missing time due to an ankle injury. There is constant fluctuation with the bench players in how much time each plays. That could cause problems.

"That's just kind of the makeup of our group, and that's special," Shamet said. "Typically, you go to a lot of NBA locker rooms, there's some ulterior motives and personal agendas — which is part of why we're all here, is some ego, of course. Everybody is a good player at this level and is striving to get to something or be somewhere. But very rarely does that take a backseat to just truly buying into one another, wanting the best because, ultimately, good things come from that for everyone. It's special. It's really special."

It can perhaps deliver more special results.

James Cook has 15 carries for only 33 yards.

Wentz is 7-of-17 for 75 yards, with Jefferson catching two for 39. Aaron Jones has three rushes for 10 yards.

#2829. Player Grades: Dallas gets third win in a row with 125-122 victory over the Pacers

The Dallas Mavericks (7-4) won a 125-122 thriller over the Indiana Pacers (3-8) on Monday night. Kyrie Irving and Cooper Flagg were dominant, combining for 78 points, while Caleb Martin made the defensive play of the game to seal the deal. On the second night of a back-to-back, the Mavericks found themselves trailing for much of the first half but worked their way back, determined to not have a letdown after a convincing win over the Brookly Nets just 24 hours prior. With the victory, the Mavericks extend their winning streak to three games.

We try to be discerning with a perfect grade, especially for a Hall of Famer who has plenty of exceptional games on his resume. Tonight Irving gets the bump despite no rebounds, steals or blocks. He was simply too dominant offensively not to. He connected on 11-of-18 from the floor and 7-of-10 from downtown. He hit 6-of-7 free throws while he was at it. Helping get him over the top was a game-high +29 plus/minus. Even with a few goose eggs in the stat line, Irving was playing on another level Monday night and did a lot in the fact of tough on-ball defense to keep the Mavs connected and ultimately able to pull away.

Little needs to be said when the box score reads as it does. Flagg hit 16-of-25 shots in a 40-point double-double and was absolutely huge down the stretch, hitting big shots in the fourth quarter in a refuse-to-lose performance. Just dominant while leaving a couple rough shooting nights as a distant memory.

The conundrum of Martin persists. A starter with limited minutes and little tangible production makes the defensive play of the night to seal the victory. We've yet to determine how best to grade him, but suffice it to say tipping the inbounds pass away from Paskal Siakam to prevent the Pacers from even attempting a shot on the final possession gives his grade a boost.

Washington gets the "5" based on some intangibles. His 4-of-12 shooting left a bit to be desired (though one of his two made three-pointers came at a critical time) and he was only 3-of-6 from the charity stripe. Of the three misses, two of them came in the waning moments where even one make would have effectively ended the game. Worse still, he probably could have gotten the ball to Irving before he was fouled, allowing the better free throw shooter to get the opportunity at the line. He rebounded well and had a few defensive efforts that don't hit the box score and the fact the outcome was a win finds us giving him a bit of a bump on his grade.

Gafford was foul-happy, playing himself off the court early on. He showed better control during the latter part of the game, but having him on the floor consistently to match up with Ivica Zubac would have helped along the way. He was solid in the limited minutes and managed to show some passing ability but it was a somewhat mundane night.

Aldama was 4-of-9 from the floor, but only 1-of-5 from downtown. Even with the longball not falling, he did a nice job maximizing his limited minutes. He had a soft touch around the rim and put himself in the right spots – especially impressive given he just returned from injury had had no prior reps with his teammates before just a couple games ago.

This was a hard-fought game that came down to the final possession. Dallas was on the second night of a back-to-back, yet got incredible offensive performances from both Flagg and Irving. The team plays together and fights hard on every possession. That isn't to say every possession is pretty, but Dallas continues to stay disciplined and tied together. On Monday night, that cohesion resulted in a great clutch win.

#2828. Green Bay Packers News: Packers prep for NFL trade deadline

Welcome to NFL Trade Deadline day! All trades need to be finalized by 4 p.m. Eastern time today as teams try to make the last-minute moves they think they need to become contenders or stockpile future assets.

We've already seen quite a few moves leading up to the deadline with a few big-name players arriving at new teams, but the eternal question in these parts is whether or not the Packers will do anything.

Certainly the Packers have needs. They could use some help on the offensive line, even as the guard situation seems to stabilize, and a running back with any amount of actual juice would be a blessing. And, if you believe the rumors going around, they've been sniffing around just about any trade-worth defensive lineman with a pulse.

But the question is whether or not any of those moves would actually fix anything for them. Would throwing a new running back behind the offensive line as it's presently constituted actually improve the running game? That seems doubtful, and I'm skeptical of the idea that they could add any linemen who would make a real difference, either. And there's also the question of price. Take Jonathan Taylor, for instance. He'd definitely be a better running back option than anything the Packers currently have, but it sounds like it's going to take a king's ransom to pry him out of Indianapolis.

The best intersection of price and value might be on the defensive line, but even then price is a huge consideration, since the Packers are already without a first round pick next year. Brian Gutekunst has gone on record about his high opinion of the 2027 draft class, and that seems to be the consensus view. Would he really surrender another valuable pick for a short-term player?

The Packers, again, undeniably have needs. But what it'd take to fix them might take them out of the trade market this year.

#2826. Player grades: Warriors vs. Pelicans

Well that was fun. The Golden State Warriors made NBA history on Monday night, by becoming the first team to start 0-3 and follow it up with an eight-game winning streak. And they certainly did it in emphatic style, as they positively crushed the New Orleans Pelicans, ending their home-stand with a 138-87 victory that was every bit as lopsided as the score would suggest.

Needless to say, the grades are going to be good for this one. As always, my grades are based on my personal expectations for each player, with a "B" grade representing that player's average performance.

Note: True-shooting percentage (TS) is a scoring efficiency metric that accounts for threes and free throws. Entering Monday's games, league-average TS was 57.1%.

21 minutes, 3 points, 7 rebounds, 4 assists, 1 block, 3 fouls, 0-for-3 shooting, 0-for-1 threes, 3-for-4 free throws, 31.5% TS, +21

You gotta love Gui. Even in a game where the Warriors were pouring in points faster than a bartender pours shots, Santos was content to just help out doing the little things. He attacked the glass and did a swell job of keeping the ball moving. He repeatedly found the open man and ended up with four dimes and zero turnovers. He was a big part of the strong defensive performance.

He just does all the little things, and even though it doesn't always come with offense, you can happily live with that on this team.

27 minutes, 23 points, 7 rebounds, 4 assists, 1 steal, 2 turnovers, 3 fouls, 8-for-10 shooting, 4-for-4 threes, 3-for-4 free throws, 97.8% TS, +34

Yeah. I think we have a star on our hands, friends. I don't think Lendeborg is good, or even really good, or even has the potential to be a star. I think he is a star, point blank. It's only been 11 games but that's abundantly clear.

There was some Steph Curry in Yax's game on Monday, in that he seemed to relish the opportunity to rip a team's soul out. So often you see rookies get sloppy when playing in a blowout. At best they hog the ball and put on their own show; at worst, they check out because the outcome is determined.

But stars like Curry lock in. They want the win to be as lopsided as possible. They want to crush the other team's spirit and make it clear that they're not in the same league (except, you know … in the literal sense). And they want to make sure that they're the one who does the damage.

Lendeborg, it seems, has that gene. He didn't try to do to much, even when the Dubs led by 20, or 30, or 40, or 50. There were no reckless heat checks or audacious dunk attempts. Instead, he just locked in like it was a tied game, and went after the Pelicans in every part of the game.

21 minutes, 2 points, 3 rebounds, 6 assists, 1 steal, 2 turnovers, 1 foul, 1-for-1 shooting, 100.0% TS, +32

Shot check! Green is up to 27 field goal attempts in nine games. There was some offseason chatter that Steve Kerr wanted Green to shoot more (specifically threes), and then it turned out the Warriors offense was good enough that Dray could be super selective, and focus on the three things he does brilliantly on that end of the court: passing the ball, setting screens, and making sure that everything runs through Curry.

Green has really been an offensive asset this year, which is a testament to his patience and playmaking, but also to the players around him. Having four shooters on the court at almost all times certainly helps there as well.

Defensively, Dray played well, though we were robbed of getting to see him defend Zion Williamson, as the Pelicans' star got the night off. Oh well; they'll meet again in a week.

Grade: APost-game bonus: Tied for the team lead in assists.

26 minutes, 25 points, 2 rebounds, 4 assists, 1 steal, 1 block, 10-for-19 shooting, 5-for-11 threes, 65.8% TS, +36

Lest you get too caught up in the Yaxel hype, Podziemski is here to remind you that there's more than one early-20s Warrior with a fun European name who just might be a star. This was Podz at his very best. He was all over the court in a blur of chaos, on both ends of the court. He attacked on offense, while also popping out time and time again, and hiding behind screens, to show off his jumper … which looks a lot better this year (he's 25-for-62 from deep so far this year).

In a fast and frantic game in which Podziemski seemed to have the ball in his hands a lot, he went a whole game with nary a turnover nor a foul.

It really feels like his offense is far more in control this year. He's always had creativity and unique explosiveness, but this year he's harnessed it far better than in year's past. Can you remember a single shot he's taken this season that has made you scratch your head or yell at the TV (except in a positive way)? I can't. He's just unbelievably in control, and fully coming into his own.

Grade: A+Post-game bonus: Tied for the team lead in points; best plus/minus on the team.

21 minutes, 25 points, 5 rebounds, 2 assists, 1 turnover, 6-for-10 shooting, 4-for-7 threes, 9-for-9 free throws, 89.5% TS, +32

Here's a fun question: who's enjoying the Lendeborg and Podziemski breakouts more, Curry or Kerr? Steph is clearly having the time of his life playing with these invigorating youngsters. And more importantly, you can see the relief in not having to carry the team on his shoulders night in and night out, and possession in and possession out.

The way that Curry is picking his spots is honestly a little reminiscent of when Klay Thompson and Kevin Durant were on the team. Curry knows he can step into his easier roles — playing the distributing point guard, or just using his gravity to space the defense out — and the offense will still function well. And then, when the time comes — if the team's in trouble, or he wants to put a nail in the coffin, or he just wants to have a little fun — he goes into supersduperduperstar mode.

He's averaging more than a point per minute with a true-shooting percentage well into the 70s. And it looks sustainable because he's not having to kill himself out there. I should give him an A+ but i can't justify a perfect grade for someone I know can — and will — pop off for 50.

#2824. Nmecha defends controversial goal celebration after criticism

Borussia Dortmund midfielder Felix Nmecha has defended his controversial goal celebration and said he doesn't want to exclude anyone with his religious belief.

"With my celebration, I don't want to put myself or any organization in the foreground. Rather, it's about putting down my "crown" in front of the soon-to-come king and point out to Jesus, my hope and my strength," Nmecha said on Instagram.

"My message was never focused on promoting intolerance, discrimination or hatred in any form."

Nmecha's recurring goal celebration, in which he takes an imaginary crown from his head and places it on the pitch in front of him while kneeling, has been criticized by Dortmund's fan department.

"Faith does not justify exclusion. Faith does not justify division. And faith should also not be misused to fail to recognize the diversity of the society in which we live," the Dortmund fan department, an official section of the club's hierarchy, said in a statement on Sunday.

"It is not about condemning a person for their faith. Our criticism is directed at religious networks that spread a worldview under the cloak of faith in which people are devalued or excluded because of their sexual orientation, their gender identity, their way of life or their personal choices."

The club has announced talks with the player and according to broadcasters WDR, citing Dortmund president Hans-Joachim Watzke, Nmecha is to refrain from celebrating the goal in that manner in the future.

Furthermore, BVB intends to contact the Ballers in God group to stop prominently advertising with the player.

Ballers in God is a network of Christian footballers founded in 2015 that records and shares many such celebrations on social media.

Nmecha has previously been criticized for religious content on social media, which has been deemed homophobic. He has rejected these accusations.
